utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-03-68-T, The Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, I would like a confirmation from you that you can follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can understand everything that is being interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning to you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Jan Wubben, senior trial attorney for the Prosecution team, together with Ms. Patricia Sellers and Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink as our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good morning to you and your team. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Vasija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones, we appear for Mr. Naser Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoffrey Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Before we bring in the witness, there are a few minor things that I would like to point out. Number one, I signed this morning the decision on the Prosecution motions to add exhibits. I would imagine it has already been filed, but that doesn't depend on me. I just wanted to inform you that I have signed it. Number two is you'll recall that either the first or the second day of hearing dealing with the Prosecution motion to submit the evidence of a particular person under Rule 92(C), we had suggested to you to try and get together and see if you could agree on a doctor, a medical doctor, who could possibly visit this person and then report back to us on particularly whether he is in a position to understood and answer questions or whether he is impaired to such extent that we can proceed with the admission of his statement, previous statement under 92(C). Do you have any news for us? Yes, Madam Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, we do have news. We discussed with Defence counsel briefly to explain what might be their wishes in terms of looking for a doctor. They had asked that we try and have a doctor that is neutral, and one possibly from Croatia or Slovenia. We've contacted our field offices. We contacted the field office in Banja Luka, and we'll contact the field office in Zagreb. The field office in Banja Luka, the Office of the Prosecutor, has forwarded the name of a neuropsychologist, neurosurgeon, and I will forward that name to the Defence counsel in the proceedings today. We would like to convey that in writing. I will note that that person, my understanding comes from Republika Srpska, it might not fulfil the wishes of the nationality of the doctor. We have not at this point in time received back from our field office in Zagreb the name of a doctor who might be of a different nationality. We will be asking the Defence in our letter, would they please possibly consider the use of this doctor, and we will wait their response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any particular problem with having a doctor from Bosnia, from Sarajevo? I would imagine there are dozens of specialised consultants - we call them consultants in my country.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can also inquire if a doctor can come from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because it will be less expensive and easier, probably. I mean, at the end of the day, we will be dealing with professional people. And I usually trust professional people.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The doctor that at this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me. The doctor that we have identified from this time comes from Zvornik, and the details will be given to the Defence in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's enough for the time being. And you let us know of any developments. The other last matter I wanted to raise relates -- did you refile the motion for the subpoena, issue of subpoena testificando?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have filed that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You haven't received -- I mean I knew that it had been filed but we haven't received a response from you. I know that time is still running. But if perhaps you can put us into the picture of whether you are still thinking about it or whether you've made up your mind already but haven't had time to file the response, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we shall file our response by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. And that's fair enough. So any other preliminary matters that you would like to raise? Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, today's witness will be cross-examined by me, and I will need the original documents. I told Mr. Jan Wubben of the OTP this, and he told me he could get them for me during the break. I apologise for not stating this earlier, but I understood from what the first witness, expert witness, said, that it is not a problem for the Prosecutor to obtain the originals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, it is not a problem, Your Honour, to obtain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But then we should know in advance, and we had then on the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But we are glad to comply with, and we accept these apologies. During the break, we will try to process that, and if we can manage during -- we need some additional time, we will inform immediately the Court manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and I thank you Madam Vidovic as well. Anything else before we admit the witness? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Dr. Koeijer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will proceed with the examination-in-chief, and then we'll move on to the cross-examination. My duty is just to remind you that you are still testifying under oath, under the solemn declaration that you entered yesterday. Please, take a seat. And we will proceed. Mr. Wubben, he is all yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. de Koeijer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Doctorandus de Koeijer, yesterday we addressed the first report, and you led us through this table with the description of the questioned documents. To be specific, the item, the type, the quality, the stamp, the features, and the similarities. And then subsequently, and this is a reiteration as a kind of introduction, Your Honour, you showed us in this enlarged stamp of Appendix 4 of the report the various aspects related to this table. And then yesterday, I should proceed on Appendix 5a, that's the part where we stopped it, Appendix 5a of the report with this group of stamps. And then we decided to break until this morning. And that's why I would like to proceed on a follow up of questions related to these pictures as shown now. My first question is, and that will also reflect in the questions regarding to all these stamps on the screen in front of you, Appendix 5a, this first stamp, left top, how do you in your professional opinion evaluate the stamp impression related to the questioned document referred to under 02075807?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, is it on the screen? Is it on the monitor now? Some technical problems, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it's okay. It's a -- problem solved. Problem solved. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Again, please, then, the stamp top left, how do you in your professional opinion, Doctorandus de Koeijer, evaluate the stamp impression related to the questioned document referred to under 02075807? And please relate your observations to the aspects from table 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. On examining this stamp impression, we saw that it was a stamp impression of reasonable quality. And we could find all four of the features we highlighted on Appendix 4 in this -- present in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay. And can you clarify further, pointing out the specific features.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, all the features mentioned in Appendix 4, features 1, 2, 3, and 4, they were all found in this stamp. And they are highlighted by the same type of markers. Furthermore, we saw that this stamp on overlaying with the reference stamp on Appendix 4 was the correct overlay. There was no mismatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I now turn to the stamp, please, on the right side, 02075809.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We also thought that this was a stamp of reasonable quality with enough detail to do the comparison. We found three of the four -- three of the four items, features in there which we had in the previous stamps also, in the stamp on Appendix 4. And these are also highlighted on the picture. Furthermore, the overlay was also correct. So there was no discrepancies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will now turn to stamp 02075808.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And Your Honour, yesterday we also discussed that in Appendix 4. So please allow me to consider this as a confirmation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And subsequently, I will turn to the next stamp. And will you please, Mr. de Koeijer, reiterate the indication of the stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The stamp 00926396 is a stamp on a photocopied document. It's a photocopied stamp also. The stamp is of reasonably poor quality, especially the centre part, although the rim is -- still has quite a few details in there. So we could still find three of the features mentioned on Appendix 4 in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Will you please give a follow up to the next stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next stamp, 01239504, is a stamp of poor quality. It was quite heavily inked, but still in the rim we could still find the features mentioned -- all four of the features mentioned in Appendix 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next stamp is stamp on document 01801583. It is of very poor quality. The document itself was a fax. This distorts the stamp quite a bit, and we could not find any of the features mentioned on Appendix 4 in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next stamp is on Document 01801585. It is a stamp again of very poor quality. Again, a fax document. And again, we could not find any of the features mentioned in Appendix 4 in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next stamp is also a stamp of very poor quality. It is on document 01801586. Again, a faxed document. And again, we could not find any features we highlighted in Appendix 4 in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I would like to proceed, Your Honours, with Appendix 5b of this report, 264.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: 5b, left top, stamp starting with 01239515. Please give me your observations and evaluation regarding table 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is an original stamp impression of reasonable quality. We found all four of the highlighted features in Appendix 4 and could make quite a reasonable comparison with this stamp. The next stamp, 01239520, is also a stamp of reasonable quality. It's an original stamp impression. And we could find three of the four rim features in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next stamp is on Document 01239521. It is a photocopied stamp impression of reasonably poor quality. We could find two of the four rim details in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next is on Document 01239522. It is also a photocopied document, and a stamp of very poor quality where we could find none of the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next stamp is on Document 01239512. It is a stamp -- an original stamp impression of poor quality. Still, we could find three of the four rim details in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next stamp is on Document 01239517. It is a stamp impression, an original stamp impression of reasonable quality. And we could find three of the four rim details in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next stamp is on Document 01239528. It is also an original stamp impression of poor quality. We could find three of the four rim details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the last one on the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's on Document 01839608. It is a stamp -- original stamp impression of poor quality. And we could find all four rim details in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I would like to turn to Appendix number 5c of the report 264. And I would like to turn to the first stamp, top left. That's 01239544 of the Appendix with ERN number 02523878.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please give your professional opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The stamp impression on Document 01239544 is an original stamp impression and of reasonable quality. And we could find all four of the rim details in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The next one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The stamp on Document 01239623 is an original stamp impression of reasonable quality, and we could find all four rim details in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the last one in this Appendix.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The stamp on 00926461 is a photocopied stamp impression of poor quality. Three of the four rim details we could find in this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This will end this Appendix, including the stamps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Doctorandus de Koeijer, I would like to turn now to the part of your report in which you clarified your findings about tampering. So my next question, that's referring to page 8 out of 10. Next question will be, Doctorandus de Koeijer, apart from these stamp impressions, did you also examine the questioned documents other than the war diary regarding tampering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And how did you examine it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We looked at a number of features. For example, we looked -- if the signatures are original or not, if they were printed or possibly stamped. We examined the stamps to see if they are original stamps. We examined also the documents for mechanical erasure of certain areas, also chemical erasure we looked for. And just a general overview of the document to see if there are any signs of tampering.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And Doctorandus de Koeijer, what were your observations as an expert when you did this examination on tampering of the questioned documents apart from the war diary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Besides the normal typing mistakes which had been corrected and obvious corrections in the document, we could find no evidence of tampering. I must comment on this that because we are not familiar with the language on the documents, it is difficult for us to on the basis of content of the document select specific areas for detailed examination of tampering. So this was a difficulty in this research.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How did you arrive to the conclusion that there is no evidence of tampering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We found no evidence of mechanical erasure, no evidence of chemical erasure. We found original, written signatures with no evidence of tracing. We found original stamps, and we only found some obvious corrected mistakes, obvious corrections. And they were not considered evidence of tampering by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will turn now to your conclusions on the stamp impressions as related on page 9 of your report. What were your final conclusions? And this, of course, regarding the similarities that you made as an expert with a view to the comparison of the stamp impressions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our final conclusions were that the stamps listed in table 1 on page 8 of the report, with a similarity index of 2, were probably produced by the same stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you please indicate what numbers you classified as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So these were the similarity score of 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These had a similarity score of 2, which meant that these were stamps of reasonable quality and had a number of features in them which allowed us to come to this conclusion that they were probably stamped by the same stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "probably produced by the same stamp"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By probably, we mean that we think that they are produced by the same stamp, but we still have reservations because the quality of the stamps were not ideal to work with. And also, we do not have the original stamp which produced these impressions. And because we do not have this original stamp, we cannot assess that the features which we looked at in this stamp impression which we considered to be damages of some sort to the rim of the stamp, that they may possibly be -- may have been there from the beginning and are not true damages but features of the original stamp as it was made. And if more than one of these stamps were made with the same features, then, yes, we cannot rule this out at the moment without examining the stamp in more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what do you mean that it might be also produced by a copy of a stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible to make a photograph of a stamp impression and use this photograph to produce a stamp exactly the same as the stamp Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. impression. So it is possible to just exactly copy a stamp from a stamp impression. And this is very -- can be very easily done by just sending a stamp impression, for example, to a specific company on the internet, and a week or two later you receive your stamp back with -- which looks like the stamp impression you have photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And further in your conclusions, you also mentioned that there is a possibility, or do you have another comment, please, on your final conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On the stamp impressions which of even less quality and possibly had even less features, we concluded that they were possibly produced by the same stamp. This is just a little less sure than the probably. It's one step down in the letter of our conclusion scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you please confirm the questioned stamp and the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And these were all the stamp impressions you made a final conclusion on, or is there more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a number of stamps we found specifically on the faxed documents and I think one of the photocopied documents which were to our opinion insufficient for comparison. They did have some general similarities, but none specific enough for us to draw a conclusion on. And these were the stamps on Documents 01801583, 01801585, 01801586, and 01239522.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will turn now to the war diary as related on page 9 of your report, Doctorandus de Koeijer. And my first question will be, did you also examine the tampering question regarding the war diary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How did you examine it? Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was -- the examination is more or less the same as the examination of the other documents, looking for mechanical and chemical erasure, looking also for evidence of -- that portions were inserted, but also we look for insertion of full pages by examining the number of pages in the specific parts of the document and by examining the thickness and the UV fluorescence of the different pages to see if there possibly had been new pages inserted into the document. Also all the pages were examined for indented writing impressions. And together with that for mechanical erasures, as this method also looks for those.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What about those inserting of pages? Because I note from your report that you talk about quires.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you further explain to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A quire is a portion of a book sewn into the back cover. It is a -- you can also call it a section. It is a bundle of pages sewn together which are sewn into the back of the cover. And usually a book consists of more than one quire. It's just to make the book stronger, that it doesn't fall apart as easy. If you put all the pages in one together, it's not strong enough. So they bundle the pages and sew them into the back cover. And one bundle of pages we call a quire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So do I take it correctly from you that such a number of pages is sealed or with a staple or a with --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- or whatever, and that such a book consists of various parts, and that's the quire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please confirm and give your comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A quire is usually either sewn in or stapled in, and that is the same for all the different quires in this book. And together, in this case, five quires made up the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And again, how many quires did you find in this war diary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And your conclusion: Were there pages inserted or not? Please give me your comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We found that the number of pages per quire differed quite -- to a large extent in these different quires. One quire had 44 pages, and another quire had had only, for example, 10 pages. What we concluded from this is that quite a number of pages had been removed from the book. We did not, however, find any -- any evidence that any pages had been inserted into the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were quite a few pages taken out, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were all these pages of the diary of the same thickness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We found that there was no -- we could not discriminate any of the pages on the basis of thickness, nor on the basis of UV fluorescence sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, would you please ask the witness on what basis did he come to the conclusion that several pages had been taken out of this diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we move to other observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, how did you come to the conclusion that some pages were taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is based on the assumption that usually in books, each quire has the same number of pages. And on this assumption, we based the conclusion that possibly quite a few pages had been removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And to finalise this, Doctorandus de Koeijer, what does your professional conclusions for tampering, including this quire examination, include regarding the war diary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could not find any definite signs of tampering on the pages remaining in the war diary. If you consider removal of pages a sign of tampering, then, well, there would possibly be tampering. But on the pages remaining in the war diary, we could not find any signs of tampering. We, again, did not consider obvious corrections present as a sign of tampering.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And in special also giving regard, attention to certain corrections, corrections you notified or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not make note of all the different corrections in the diary as there were so many. We just went through them in our examination, and of course the language is, again, a problem. So we could not identify if these corrections were just normal writing mistakes or if they were evidence of tampering in this case and really trying -- but as the corrections were quite obvious, we did not consider them signs of tampering because it was still possible to read what was there before. We just often strike through words or so you could read still what was there. So we did not consider this signs of tampering.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So that's your conclusion is clear, no definite signs of tampering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This finalises this part of the examination regarding the first report, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Witness, I have a question with regard to the quire. Is it correct to assume that if you have a quire which comes from a paper factory, that quire contains a certain number of pages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And if you take one out, there should remain something, some evidence that at this point, a page has been taken out or at another point something has been taken out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Often if pages are sewn in, if you tear out one page, another one falls out, yes. And we did not -- as far as I recollect, we did not find any loose pages in the diary. Often -- sorry. Often we will look for evidence of pages being -- which have been removed using indented impressions, examination. However, the paper in the diary was of reasonably poor quality, and this does not -- well, we had problems doing this type of examination on this paper. So sometimes we did find some impressions, and most often we found very little impressions. So I cannot definitely say that pages were removed. This is purely based on the assumption that we normally see that the number of pages per quire is the same throughout the whole book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a second question. If you take out a page after a book has been filled with writing, then it may be normal that the connection between page 1 and 3 would not fit together somehow. So even if you do not know the language, did you recognise any discontinuancy between the contents of, let's say, page 1 and the next page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe it was examined in this detail, this examination was done.

utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.text: Then I would like if you allow me, Your Honour, to take this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We see this number at the end of the sentence "features in the stamp impression on document." And does that number refer to the overview of the reference and questioned material submitted to you and as I referred to in the beginning, to page 2 of your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.text: How can the Judges know what reference to what questioned material this number is referring to?

utterances.text: On page 2 of the -- in the table on page 2 of the report, the number is mentioned. And behind the number in the second column is mentioned item Q25. And the description of the exhibit is mentioned in the third column. So the numbers refer to the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And does that method of referring also apply in appendix that gives an overview of stamps and their impressions and numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please turn now to Appendix 4, ERN number top right 03594736, Your Honour. To be clear, to confirm, will you confirm that the numbers seen left above each of these stamp pictures refer to the related questioned documents examined by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How did you compare the round stamp impressions on the questioned documents for your examination as an expert?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We compared it in the same way as the other stamp impressions in the previous case. We used in this case the stamp impression on Document 01239545, that is the top left stamp impression on appendix 4, as a reference stamp. So not the stamp impression on Appendix 3. We superimposed all the other stamp impressions on top of this stamp in a digital fashion after scanning them in on the computer. This -- during this superimposition, we looked to see if the stamps matched in general shape and form and also in detail. Furthermore, we will examine the stamps with the microscope to examine the detail more closely. And also to determine if it is an original stamp or a copy or, for example, a printed stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's now turn to this Appendix 3, the features in the stamp impression on 03557343, again with the ERN number top right 03594735. What does your -- what does your professional opinion tell you or comment you on this picture of Appendix 4 referring to that number showing -- to show details of the stamp impression? Again, we are here at Appendix Number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This stamp impression is a -- this is a photocopy of a stamp impression of reasonable quality. As we can see, still quite a lot of detail, for example, in the rim of the stamp. Some of the detail is missing in the middle. But in this stamp, we could identify at least four specific details which we could also see in quite a few of the other stamps. And they are highlighted 1, 2, 3, and 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will turn to -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Wubben. Because I think we need to make this clear. Did the witness try to find on this specimen the same distinctive points or features that he identified in the previous specimen that he used for the purpose of the first report? In other words, did he stick to the same features, trying to find them also on one of these stamps that then he used as a specimen, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is correct. Why did you have to choose another one from amongst these and not stick to the one you had used previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we were not asked to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay, I get you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- to link it to the previous case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, okay. I get you. All right. Go ahead, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will now refer to this table 1, table 1 in your report. And that's the table with the aspects and columns. Earlier you clarified this, page 7 of the report with the ERN number 03594725. And earlier you clarified the various aspects of the column, the item, the type, the quality of the stamp, the features, the similarities. Does that clarification and confirmation also apply to this column -- this report, sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, I would like to turn again to this stamp of Appendix 3 of P265. Appendix 3, again. And will you then apply -- confirm to the Judges what these table 1 aspects tell you about this stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we look at table 1 concerning this stamp, we see that the type -- the type of document is a photocopy, that the stamp is of reasonable quality, and that it has the features 1, 2, 3, and 4 visible in the stamp. And we concluded from that a similarity index of 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Meaning that, when I ask your professional opinion initially, you will always do it from the aspects of the table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let's turn then to the group of stamps you examined and Appendix Number 4, stamp impressions of the other questioned documents. To start with, on this page, ERN on top right 03594736, you start with the stamp, and left above the stamp 01239545, I would like to ask your professional comment how you evaluate as an expert the stamp impression related to the questioned document referred to and what can you tell us about these type and aspects referred to in table 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This stamp impression is an original stamp impression of reasonable quality. In the stamp impression, we could identify three of the four features mentioned in Appendix 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And will you please proceed per stamp impression and starting with the number referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. The stamp impression on Document 01787786 is also an original stamp impression with the general aspects of the other stamps examined. It is of poor quality, only we could not find any of the specific parts -- damages to the rim we highlighted in Appendix 3. The stamp impression on Document 02075810 is also an original stamp impression of reasonable quality. We found two of the four features mentioned on Appendix 3. The stamp impression on Document 03557343 is a photocopied stamp and is the same stamp as on Appendix 3. So skip that one probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It's a confirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And the stamp impression on Document 03720936 is a photocopied stamp impression of poor quality. And we found two of the four features. The stamp impression on Document 03721234 is a photocopied stamp impression, and we found two of the four features. The stamp impression on Document 03721253 is a photocopied stamp impression of reasonable quality. We found three of the four features. The stamp impression on Document 03721400 is a photocopied stamp impression of reasonable quality. And we found two of the four features. Of really poor quality, I mean. The stamp impression of -- on Document 03721482 is a photocopied stamp impression, very poor quality. We could not identify any of the features. The stamp impression on Document 03721483 is also a very poor quality photocopied stamp impression, and we could identify two of the four features.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Before, Mr. Wubben, before he proceeds any further, perhaps a simple explanation. I am looking at table 1, just as you should be, sir. And in relation to the penultimate entry, that is, the item with ERN number 03721482, in your testimony you said -- you mentioned photocopy. Here we have ballpoint.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's an error in the table. Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we should replace it with "photocopy."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With "photocopy," yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Apart from the stamp impression, did you also examine the questioned documents regarding tampering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How did you examine, please, and I refer to page 7 of the report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was done in the same manner as the -- in the previous case, looking for mechanical erasures, chemical erasure, and nonoriginal signatures and nonoriginal stamps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What observations did you make regarding this possible tampering or not of the questioned documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We found no evidence of tampering. And again, we did not consider obvious corrections, evidence of tampering.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How did you arrive on this conclusion, opinion of no evidence of tampering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could find no evidence of mechanical erasure, nor chemical erasure. We saw that the -- on the original documents, they were original stamps, original signatures. And there was no general evidence of tampering found.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, I will turn to the final conclusions regarding the stamp impressions. Doctorandus de Koeijer, as an expert, what final conclusions did you draw with a view to the comparison of stamp impressions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conclusions we drew from the examination are the following: The stamp impressions on the documents listed in table 1 which showed a similarity index of 2, we said are probably produced by the same stamp or a copy of this stamp. The examination -- the examined impressions on the documents listed in table 1 with a similarity index of 1 we concluded are possibly produced by the same stamp or a copy of this stamp. And the impression listed on -- in table 1 by an X, similarity index of X, we concluded that this -- although the stamp showed the same general features, it showed no evidence of the detailed features. And whilst we would expect them to be there, given the quality of the stamp, that it was possibly -- and it was therefore possibly produced by another stamp of similar type without the same wear features.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what do you mean by this conclusion "probably produced by the same stamp or a copy of the stamp"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We mean by this conclusion that it is possible to make an exact copy of a stamp impression and use this newly made stamp to reproduce a stamp impression. So it can almost been not possible for an examiner to identify any differences between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what do you mean by the score "possibly produced" and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Possibly produced," we mean this is the least -- the lowest level of -- positive level of our conclusion scale. We mean it could be produced by this stamp, but there are just a small number of features. We cannot rule out that it was possibly -- that it would have been produced by another stamp of the same type. And we can just -- we would need to examine the original stamp to be able to come to a higher conclusion in these impressions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I come to the finalisation of my questions, Your Honour. But when I look at the chapter of tampering, I see at that, tampering in bold, the last sentence of -- the last line of that paragraph is referring to 8545. And prior to that, 0123. utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Whether or not I'm correct, or if so, please comment, this number 01238545 is a typo and should be read as 9545? Please take your time to compare.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you explain again where this mistake --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me explain it in my own terms. You refer in looking at page 8 of your report, the second line from the top. You have in square brackets 0123-9545.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, that would correspond to one of the documents you have referred to earlier as having been examined by you. If you look at table 1, it's the fourth one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you go down further in the page under the section titled "tampering."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a part called "tampering," fourth line, which is the last line of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.
